channel.title: Hastings Daily: Community & people
channel.description: Local news for Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill and Battle, three times a day.

item.title: Hastings couple to mark 70th Platinum wedding anniversary
item.description: A Hastings couple is to celebrate its 70th, or Platinum, wedding anniversary next month.

item.title: Liane Carroll to give Christmas concert at St Clement's for the Sara Lee Trust
item.description: Award-winning jazz artist Liane Carroll is to give a Christmas concert in Hastings to raise vital funds for the Sara Lee Trust, the local cancer charity.

item.title: Rye Town Clerk honoured with the town's highest civic award
item.description: Richard Farhall has been made an Honorary Freeman of the Ancient Town of Rye, the town's highest civic award, in recognition of his 26 years of service as Rye Town Clerk.

item.title: St Leonards Frost Fair returns on November 28 with Snow Queen parade
item.description: The St Leonards Frost Fair returns on Saturday 28 November with a parade of colourful fairy-tale characters, led by the Snow Queen, processing through the streets.

item.title: Donations top £10,000 for Isfield farm shop after raid
item.description: Donations totalling more than £10,000 have flowed in to help a family farm in Isfield after thieves ransacked its shop, the owners said.

item.title: Bexhill Leisure Centre named UK Active Awards finalist
item.description: Bexhill Leisure Centre has been named a finalist for Regional Centre of the Year at the UK Active Awards, one of the leisure industry's leading national award programmes.

item.title: Little Common Library marks annual volunteer lunch
item.description: Volunteers and supporters came together in Bexhill for Little Common Library's annual fish and chip lunch, its chairman Connor Winter said.

item.title: Battle Bonfire 2026: 'Guy Feaux' effigy takes a swipe at AI
item.description: Battle High Street became a 'river of fire' on Saturday night as people turned out for the town's annual bonfire celebrations, the Hastings Observer reported.

item.title: Rye Bonfire named among the UK's best Bonfire Night displays
item.description: The Rye and District Bonfire has been named among the best Bonfire Night displays in the country, The Argus reports.

item.title: Hastings brothers set for Nepal peaks for veterans' charity
item.description: Two brothers from Hastings are heading to the Himalayas to raise money for a local veterans' charity.

item.title: Westfield player Michael Rwabigwi called up for Rwanda
item.description: A player at a tenth-tier English football club has been called up to represent his country.

item.title: St Leonards' Becky Palmer wins Christmas tree flinging at Catsfield
item.description: A 27-year-old from St Leonards has won the women's title at the Christmas tree flinging contest at Catsfield Christmas Tree Farm near Battle.

item.title: Swansea Sound to open tour at The Piper in St Leonards
item.description: Swansea Sound, who feature members of Heavenly and Talulah Gosh, are to kick off their tour in St Leonards at The Piper on 13 November.

item.title: Local band raises £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless
item.description: A group of local musicians have raised around £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless in the last couple of years by giving their CDs away free and encouraging audiences to donate to the charity instead.

item.title: Hastings swimmer plots route to 2028 Channel crossing
item.description: Hastings swimmer Sarah Milne has completed an endurance training camp in Dover with The King's Swimmers and, in her latest diary for the Hastings Independent Press, says she is now preparing for a solo Channel crossing attempt in 2028.

item.title: Hastings runner to take on 55-mile ultramarathon in jeans
item.description: A 21-year-old from Hastings is about to take on one of the country's toughest challenges, and he is doing it in denim.

item.title: MP joins launch of Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal
item.description: Helena Dollimore, the MP for Hastings, Rye and the villages, has joined veterans and volunteers at the launch of this year's Hastings & St Leonards Poppy Appeal, held in Tesco, raising money for veterans and their families.

item.title: Ada the Asda car park fox has been relocated to a safer home
item.description: Ada, the friendly fox that made her home in an Asda car park in Hastings, has been moved to a safer place by a wildlife charity. The fox had become well known for approaching shoppers, begging for food and trying to climb up people's legs.

item.title: Bexhill mayor celebrates new school councillors at Glenleigh Park Primary
item.description: Glenleigh Park Primary Academy in Bexhill hosted a special assembly to celebrate student leadership, with the Mayor of Bexhill, Cllr Memish Huseyin, in attendance. The visit marked the appointment of the school's newly elected school and eco councillors, following an election campaign that involved all pupils.

item.title: Seagull artist's gull-version masterpieces on show in Crown pub
item.description: Hastings artist Bill Greenhead, known for his cartoon-style paintings of chip-stealing seagulls, has an exhibition in the Snug bar of the Crown in Hastings Old Town.

item.title: Sculptor Leigh Dyer's steel fins go on sale at At Sea
item.description: The metal sculptor behind several well-known works around Hastings has opened a new line for sale at the At Sea gallery in the Old Town.

item.title: BFI film course sees 18 young people make their first film in St Leonards
item.description: A group of 18 young people under 19 have taken part in a six-day film course in St Leonards, making an original short film from scratch as part of the BFI Film Academy South East Introductory Course.

item.title: GP link worker helping Hastings residents with long-term conditions get active
item.description: Active Hastings' specialised 'Link Worker' is helping residents with long-term health conditions become more active, bridging the gap between healthcare and community-based activity, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: From Hastings to the Royal Albert Hall: Count Us IN set to perform
item.description: Fifty-one young musicians from Hastings and St Leonards will take the stage at the Royal Albert Hall on 10 November as part of the Music for Youth Proms.

item.title: Hastings care home rated 'Good' across all five CQC areas
item.description: Mountside Care Home in Hastings has been rated 'Good' in all five areas assessed by the Care Quality Commission.

item.title: Bexhill family featured in Chestnut Tree House hospice film
item.description: The family of a six-year-old Bexhill boy who died of a brain condition has featured in a new film as part of a campaign to show the vital role of hospices.

item.title: 'Write by the River' poetry exhibition opens at Rye station
item.description: A new poetry and artwork exhibition called 'Write by the River' has opened at Rye railway station. It features poems and illustrations about the area's waterways, including the River Rother and River Tillingham.

item.title: Storms strip Pett Level beach, exposing 1940s sea wall
item.description: Storms Austen and Boelo have stripped away large sections of Pett Level's shingle beach defences, exposing for the first time in decades an old 1940s stepped concrete sea wall and a tarmac service road that had been buried beneath the shingle, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: Hastings' last wooden fishing boat 'Felicity' to be restored and displayed in Rock-a-Nore
item.description: The last surviving wooden fishing boat from Hastings is to be restored and put on permanent display after a fund-raising campaign reached its target of £5,000. The 'Felicity', RX58, will be displayed on the piece of land opposite the Dolphin pub in Rock-a-Nore Road.

item.title: Ark Alexandra CCF wins three honours at Lord-Lieutenant's Awards
item.description: Ark Alexandra Academy's Combined Cadet Force had a triple win at the Lord-Lieutenant's Awards Ceremony, held at Lancing College and attended by senior military personnel and civic representatives from across the region.

item.title: Rye station to close from 3pm for bonfire celebrations
item.description: Southern has announced that Rye railway station will be closed from 3pm on the day of the town's bonfire celebrations, Saturday, 14 November, until the regular start of service the next day, Sunday.

item.title: Former St Leonards church becomes community hub with weekly market
item.description: A former church in St Leonards has become a thriving community hub, hosting a popular weekly market and serving as a venue for concerts and events.

item.title: Toilets top of residents' list in £21.5m Pride in Place survey
item.description: New toilets have topped the list of improvements residents want in Hastings, after MP Helena Dollimore asked how the £21.5 million of Government Pride in Place funding should be spent.

item.title: Charity raises £4,000 to save Bexhill Hospital stroke rehabilitation service
item.description: Becky, Sarah and Owen from the #DoItForJosh charity met the team at Bexhill Hospital’s Irvine Unit on Monday to mark the continuation of a vital local stroke rehabilitation programme.

item.title: Westfield says farewell to Christmas Lights co-founder Ken Munday BEM
item.description: Westfield, outside Hastings, has paid its respects to Ken Munday, who was awarded the British Empire Medal for his services to the village.

item.title: Bird deaths spark campaign to remove netting in Hastings and Rother
item.description: A new local campaign is calling for safer ways to manage birds around buildings after three incidents in which birds became trapped in netting.

item.title: Residents brand St Leonards metal supports an 'eyesore'
item.description: Residents have branded large metal supports in St Leonards an 'eyesore'.

item.title: Battle Bonfire returns to the Abbey Green on Saturday
item.description: Battle holds what is said to be the oldest Guy Fawkes bonfire celebrations in England on Saturday 7 November, with the town's tradition tracing back to 1646. St Mary's Church then allocated two shillings and sixpence for gunpowder treason rejoicing, and the Battel Bonfire Boyes have kept the custom alive ever since.

item.title: Bexhill care home wins Pet Friendly Care Home Award
item.description: Elizabeth Court Rest Home in Hastings Road, Bexhill, has won the Pet Friendly Care Home Award for 2026. The home, which provides residential care for older people, lets its residents bring their own pets with them when they move in.

item.title: Free off-grid solar workshops coming to Hastings and Battle
item.description: Energise Sussex Coast, a local community benefit society, is holding free workshops on off-grid solar power in Hastings and Battle this month. The sessions are aimed at anyone who wants to build a small, fully off-grid solar system for a shed, workshop, van or truck, and no technical background is needed.

item.title: Martin Cohen to launch new book at Hastings Palestine Solidarity event
item.description: Bestselling philosophy writer Martin Cohen is returning to Hastings to launch his latest book on Wednesday 11 November.

item.title: Hastings joins in the 'Dusking' morris-dancing tradition
item.description: A new autumn ritual called 'Dusking' has reached the Hastings seafront, bringing morris dancing to the town's darkening days.

item.title: Beachy Head naval battle book published posthumously
item.description: The final book from late Shoreham-based lawyer Quintin Barry, Beachy Head 1690: The Grand Alliance at Bay, has been published after his death in January 2025, aged 88.

item.title: Christmas Makers' Fair at De La Warr Pavilion on 7 November
item.description: Bexhill Artists' Workspace is holding its Christmas Makers' Fair at The Studio, De La Warr Pavilion, Bexhill, on Saturday 7 November.

item.title: Iden's The Bell pub moves closer to reopening after plans submitted
item.description: A village pub that has been closed for years could reopen with three new guest rooms, after renovation plans were submitted to Rother District Council.

item.title: Status Quo's Francis Rossi to play De La Warr Pavilion, Bexhill
item.description: Francis Rossi is to bring his solo Status Quo show to Bexhill this month. The guitarist will perform his Songbook: Quo – Past, Present, Future tour at the De La Warr Pavilion on Tuesday, November 10, the Sussex Express reports.

item.title: Local author Elizabeth Webb's new novel reviewed
item.description: A new book by locally based author Elizabeth Webb has been reviewed by Michael Salmon in the Hastings Online Times. Dexter's Lot, published by BiblioMuso, follows its protagonist as he stumbles "from the exciting world of rock music to the mundane world of the supermarket," enduring many trials along the way.

item.title: Dee Day White retires after 34 years running yard in Courthouse Street
item.description: Dee Day White is retiring after running a popular antique and bric-a-brac mews and yard in Courthouse Street, Hastings Old Town, for the past 34 years.

item.title: St Michael's Hospice opens Festive Market in St Leonards
item.description: St Michael's Hospice is holding a two-day Festive Market at its Upper Maze Hill site in St Leonards on Saturday, November 14, and Sunday, November 15.

item.title: Ocean Symposium returns to Bexhill in November
item.description: Bexhill is to host an Ocean Symposium and Marine Exhibition at St Peter's Community Centre on Saturday, November 14.
